benchmark_details.name: Company Lists
benchmark_details.overview: Models extract company names and locations from printed member lists and trade indexes of the British Chamber of Commerce for Switzerland, 1921–1958, held by the Swiss Economic Archives; the pages change layout and are in English and German.

purpose_and_intended_users.goal: Measure how well vision-language models turn printed directory pages with changing layouts (alphabetical directories, thematic trade indexes, one or two columns) into a list of entries with company name and location. The results are meant to guide historians, archivists and digital humanities projects in choosing a model for extracting serial records from printed directories, for example as a first step towards georeferencing firms.
tasks: entry segmentation on printed list pages
extraction of company names and locations
purpose_and_intended_users.limitations: The 15 pages come from one publication series, mostly in English with German headings and company names in several languages; results do not transfer to other directories. Addresses, telephone numbers and product descriptions are not extracted, because not every entry has them. Entries are compared by position (see Calculation), so a skipped, merged or extra entry shifts every later entry and turns correct extractions into mismatches; reading a two-column page in a different order has the same effect. The ground truth also contains `page_id` and `entry_id`, whose expected values are the image basename and `<page_id>-<n>`. Both prompts contain a literal `{page_id}` placeholder that the benchmark does not fill (it implements no `get_prompt_kwargs`), so the model is never given these values. `prompt.txt` also shows malformed JSON and describes an array, while the schema requires a `ListPage` object. These inconsistencies penalise otherwise correct content extraction.
out_of_scope_uses: drawing conclusions about the firms or persons listed
evaluating full-text OCR of directory pages
treating a score as company-name/location accuracy alone, because identifiers are also scored

data.source: Trade indexes of the British Chamber of Commerce for Switzerland, issued 1921–1958, held by the Swiss Economic Archives (Schweizerisches Wirtschaftsarchiv), shelf mark UBW Zo 1394, digitised on e-manuscripta: https://doi.org/10.7891/e-manuscripta-174832. The complete record comprises 14 indexes; each lists the chamber's members, first as an alphabetical directory with page references, then as a trade index with full entries (addresses, locations and, in later years, telephone numbers and telegraphic codes).
data.annotation: The annotators Lea Kasper and Sorin Marti created the ground truth, with Lea Kasper as domain expert. No annotation guidelines are recorded beyond the [prompt file](prompts/prompt.txt).
data.collection_date: Source documents: 1921–1958. Added to the benchmark: October 2025.
data.contamination_controls: None. The scans, prompts and ground truth have been public in this repository since October 2025.

methods: zero-shot structured extraction from a single image per request, temperature 0.5
structured JSON output requested using the `ListPage` dataclass

two prompt variants: [prompt.txt](prompts/prompt.txt) describes the source, the two list types and the output fields; [prompt_min.txt](prompts/prompt_min.txt) only asks for valid JSON and leaves the structure to the dataclass
output cap: the repository default of 16,384 tokens per request
methodology.calculation:
A response that is a bare list is wrapped as `entries`. Every terminal field of the JSON is then compared between response and ground truth by its path, for example `entries[3].company_name`; fields under `metadata` are ignored. `null`, `"null"` and missing values count as empty. Values are compared with the rapidfuzz `fuzz.ratio` similarity scaled to 0–1; a field is a match at 0.92 or above.

- TP: both have a value and the score is at least 0.92
- FP and FN: both have a value but the score is below 0.92 (the field counts once as each)
- FP: only the response has a value
- FN: only the ground truth has a value

F1 per page is rounded to two decimals. F1 macro averages the rounded per-page F1; F1 micro sums TP, FP and FN over all scored pages before computing F1 and is not rounded. A response that does not parse is not scored and enters neither aggregate.
methodology.interpretation: Scores range from 0 to 1; higher is better. The identifier fields are scored but their values are never given to the model, so perfect company names and locations with non-matching identifiers score about 0.63 (see Baseline Results); this is not a hard maximum, as a model that produces the expected identifiers scores higher. Compare the descriptive and minimal prompts separately, because they give different instructions.
methodology.baseline_results:
Results are on the [benchmark page](https://rise-services.rise.unibas.ch/benchmarks/p/benchmarks/company_lists) and in `results/<date>/<test_id>/` at the repository root. No fixed baseline is recorded. Compare runs only with the same prompt, rules and ground-truth revision, and report the number of scored pages with the score. A diagnostic response that copies every company name and location in the correct order but sets all page and entry identifiers to `wrong` scores macro F1 0.628 and micro F1 0.629032 across the 15 pages.

Observed across models: allowing for the identifier fields the model is not given (see Interpretation; the best stored score is 0.61), most models handle the English directory layouts well. Pages that break the entry order, notably two-column German thematic lists, score near zero for many models, because entries are compared by position.
methodology.validation: The ground truth was created by the annotators and the domain expert named under Annotation; no separate check is recorded. Scoring is deterministic; the scorer is covered by the repository's test suite.
methodology.validity_justification: Field-level F1 reflects the downstream use: each entry becomes a database record whose name and location must be usable for georeferencing.

ethical_and_legal_considerations.privacy_and_anonymity: The pages list firms; some entries are sole proprietors named as persons (for example `Adolf Bürgin`). The entries give business names and locations only, from printed directories published 1921–1958. Nothing is anonymised.
ethical_and_legal_considerations.compliance_with_regulations: The indexes are printed publications held by the Swiss Economic Archives, which publishes the scans on e-manuscripta under the Public Domain Mark 1.0. No separate reuse terms are stated for the ground truth. No ethical review was carried out.
